issues.legal_issue: A will cannot be accepted as valid when suspicious circumstances surrounding its execution and attestation remain unexplained by the person relying on it.
material_facts: The will disinherited some natural heirs without stating a reason.
The initial written statement filed by the legatees did not mention the will; it was first mentioned in an additional written statement after another heir was added as a defendant.
The Sub-Registrar could not say whether the Lambardar who identified the executant was the person claimed by the District Judge to have done so.
The scribe testified that he did not know the executant.
The courts below found that the suspicious circumstances had not been dispelled to their satisfaction.
issues.conclusion: The will was not accepted as valid, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, leaving the concurrent decisions below undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The person propounding a will must satisfy the court that it was executed and attested as required by the Indian Succession Act, 1925, and that it was the product of the testator’s free volition, executed voluntarily with knowledge and understanding of its contents. When suspicious circumstances exist, the propounder must dispel them. The Court relied on Rani Purnima Debi v. Kumar Khagendra Narayan Deb (AIR 1962 SC 567), which relied on an earlier decision reported at AIR 1959 SC 443.

rule.if: will_validity_proceeding and suspicious_circumstances and not suspicions_dispelled

predicates.will_validity_proceeding: A court proceeding concerns whether a will should be accepted as valid.
predicates.suspicious_circumstances: Circumstances surrounding the will’s execution or attestation raise suspicion about its genuineness or validity.
predicates.suspicions_dispelled: The person relying on the will satisfactorily explains the suspicious circumstances.
predicates.will_not_accepted_as_valid: The will is not accepted as valid.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a will, suspicious circumstances exist, and the person relying on it has not satisfactorily explained them, the will is not accepted as valid.

issues.legal_issue: Registration of a will alone does not dispel suspicious circumstances concerning its validity.
material_facts: The will was registered, and the Sub-Registrar recorded that the executant was introduced to him and admitted and signed the execution in his presence.
The courts below nevertheless identified suspicious circumstances concerning the will’s execution and found that they had not been dispelled.
issues.conclusion: The will’s registration did not remove the unresolved suspicions, and the decision rejecting it as valid was left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rani Purnima Debi v. Kumar Khagendra Narayan Deb (AIR 1962 SC 567), registration by itself is insufficient to dispel suspicions where they exist; a general statement by a witness that the testator admitted execution is likewise insufficient to establish due execution and attestation. That decision relied on an earlier decision reported at AIR 1959 SC 443.
